security_audit.summary: All 65 static matches are false positives for Markdown formatting, fixed documentation references, or standard Git worktree examples. Semantic review identifies broad permissions with automatic approvals, incomplete read-only enforcement, and cleanup without explicit ownership verification. No evidence found of audit manipulation, credential theft, or malicious exfiltration in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Broad CLI permissions and automatic approval reduce user control over delegated actions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization for each provider and write task; restrict permitted commands and avoid automatic approval flags by default.

remediation.issue: Read-only guidance does not consistently enforce filesystem restrictions.
remediation.suggestion: Use verified provider-specific read-only controls or operating-system restrictions; test write denial and do not present a Git worktree as a security sandbox.

remediation.issue: Cleanup relies on filename patterns without an explicit ownership record.
remediation.suggestion: Record files before execution, track agent-created artifacts, and require confirmation before deleting any unverified file.

semantic_findings.title: Broad CLI Permissions Combined With Automatic Approval
semantic_findings.description: The guide allows all arguments through 'Bash(codex:*)', 'Bash(gemini:*)', and 'Bash(cursor-agent:*)'. It also recommends '--yolo' and '--force', reducing approval barriers for delegated commands and file changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission patterns are explicit, and the Cursor write example is labeled 'auto-approves'. This is unsafe delegation guidance, not evidence of malicious author intent.

semantic_findings.title: Read-Only Guidance Lacks Consistent Enforcement
semantic_findings.description: The guide labels 'gemini --sandbox --yolo' and 'cursor-agent -p' as read-only, then relies on 'Do NOT modify any files' prompts. Sandboxing and approval behavior alone do not establish filesystem write denial; a Git worktree also does not confine an agent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The read-only labels and prompt-only restriction are directly visible. The supplied guide provides no verification that Gemini or Cursor writes are actually denied.

semantic_findings.title: Cleanup Guidance Lacks Explicit Artifact Ownership Checks
semantic_findings.description: Default cleanup instructs readers to 'Delete agent-created files' and supplies broad patterns such as '*_analysis.json'. No explicit baseline or ownership record distinguishes agent artifacts from other new files, risking accidental deletion during concurrent work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prose requires new-file checks and reading before deletion, but it does not define how ownership is verified. The risk concerns following this guidance; no deletion implementation is supplied.

content.user_title: Coordinate Tasks Across AI Coding Providers
content.value_statement: Delegating work across AI providers requires consistent routing, execution, and result collection. This guide documents native Task delegation, provider selection, parallel workflows, and authentication recovery.
actual_capabilities: Documents external Codex, Gemini, and Cursor CLI invocation through Claude Code Task agents.
Provides provider selection rules based on task complexity, context size, sandbox needs, speed, and budget.
Shows parallel Task invocation and blocking or nonblocking TaskOutput collection.
Describes authentication failure detection, interactive terminal login, and invocation retry.
Provides Git worktree workflows for separating agent changes and reviewing them before merging.
Documents fallback chains and responses to rate limits and timeouts.
limitations: This package contains documentation, not an executable orchestration service.
Referenced provider cookbooks, setup commands, and terminal helpers are not included in the reviewed package.
Native Task examples depend on Claude Code tooling, installed provider CLIs, permissions, and active authentication.
Read-only labels require verification; model names, context limits, and CLI flags may become outdated.

use_cases.title: Compare Independent Code Reviews
use_cases.description: Plan parallel reviews with separate providers, collect their findings, and reconcile differences before making changes.

use_cases.title: Route Architecture Analysis
use_cases.description: Select providers according to reasoning complexity, context size, and budget while defining a fallback sequence.

use_cases.title: Plan Controlled Agent Execution
use_cases.description: Define authentication recovery, worktree separation, result collection, and approval checkpoints for delegated development tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a provider for reviewing this function using the documented routing rules. Explain your choice and list prerequisites. Do not execute commands.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Read-Only Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Codex review of [files]. Verify installed CLI help and read-only enforcement. Request approval before invocation and return findings without file changes.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Reviews
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan parallel Codex and Gemini reviews of [component]. Confirm provider consent and write restrictions. After approval, collect results and summarize agreements and disagreements.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Controlled Delegation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a delegation workflow for [task] with provider routing, fallback, authentication recovery, separate worktrees, artifact ownership tracking, and approval before writes or merges.

output_examples.input: Select a provider for a review that requires filesystem write denial.
output: Recommended provider: Codex, based on the cookbook sandbox routing rule.
Prerequisites: installed CLI, authentication, current help output, and verified read-only controls.
Execution status: awaiting approval; no files changed.

output_examples.input: Plan parallel architecture and security reviews without changing the repository.
output: Architecture review: Gemini, subject to provider consent and verified write restrictions.
Security review: Codex with verified read-only controls.
Collection plan: monitor both tasks, wait for completion, and compare findings.
Recovery plan: request interactive login if authentication fails, then retry the approved task.

best_practices: Verify installed CLI help, model availability, permissions, and authentication before constructing commands.
Obtain provider consent and enforce filesystem restrictions; do not rely on prompts or worktrees as security boundaries.
Review results before merging and delete only artifacts with verified ownership.
anti_patterns: Granting wildcard CLI permissions and automatic approval without defining permitted actions.
Treating a read-only prompt, generic sandbox, or Git worktree as proof that writes are impossible.
Deleting matching filenames without confirming that the current agent created them.

faq.question: Does this skill execute tasks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples for manual delegation through compatible tools.

faq.question: Which providers have invocation examples?
faq.answer: The native invocation guide includes Codex, Gemini, and Cursor examples. The routing cookbook also discusses Claude.

faq.question: Can I use every example directly in Codex?
faq.answer: No. Native Task and TaskOutput examples depend on Claude Code. Other environments require adapting the documented workflow.

faq.question: Are all dependencies included?
faq.answer: No. Several referenced cookbooks, setup commands, provider tools, and terminal helpers are outside the reviewed package.

faq.question: Does read-only mode guarantee that files cannot change?
faq.answer: No. Verify filesystem write denial for each provider. Prompt instructions and Git worktrees do not enforce it.

faq.question: What happens when authentication fails?
faq.answer: The guide recommends opening an interactive terminal for provider login, waiting for completion, and retrying the task.
